questions.solutionHtml:
Notochord

Chordoma is a rare slow growing neoplasm thought to arise from cellular remnants of the notochord.



Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice 42nd, Page No. 567.

questions.stem: Pain referred to ear in case of tonsillitis is due to:
questions.solutionHtml:
Glossopharyngeal nerve

Referred pain in ear occurs Via Glossopharyngeal nerve [cranial nerve IX]: This comes from the oropharynx, and can be due to pharyngitis, pharyngeal ulceration, tonsillitis, or to carcinoma of the oropharynx (base of tongue, soft palate, pharyngeal wall, tonsils).



BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 3, Page No. 261.

questions.stem: About Sibson’s fascia all are true except:

options.label: A
options.text: Attached to the inner border of 2nd rib

questions.answerText: Attached to the inner border of 2nd rib
questions.solutionHtml:
Attached to the inner border of 2nd rib

The suprapleural membrane is also known as Sibson’s fascia, it is attached to the first rib.

Suprapleural membrane is:

  • Dome-shaped musculofascial expansion
  • Muscular part – scalenus minimus muscle
  • Fascial part – endothoracic fascia.


Gray's Anatomy:The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice 42nd, Page No. 578.

questions.stem: Structure not passing through aortic opening:
questions.solutionHtml:
IVC
  • The inferior vena cava passes through the diaphragm at the vena caval foramen. This aperture is located in the central tendon at the level of T8.
  • Sometimes the phrenic nerve may also be found passing through this aperture. The esophageal hiatus is located in the muscular aspect of the diaphragm near the right crus.


BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 1, Page No. 216.

questions.stemHtml: What is the action of this Muscle (pointed) at metacarpophalangeal joint?
questions.solutionHtml:
Flexion

The lumbricals perform movements of the second to fifth finger. Their contraction leads to flexion at the metacarpophalangeal joints (MCP) and extension at both proximal (PIP) and distal interphalangeal joints (DIP).

  • The reason for the opposite actions is that the tendons cross the MCP on the palmar side, but distally insert at the dorsal side of the finger.
  • These combined movements support a strong hand grip (e.g. holding a pen).
  • The muscle pointed is the first lumbrical which will flex the second MCP joint and extend the PIP and DIP joints of the index finger.


BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 1, Page No. 130,131.

questions.stem: Special visceral efferent fiber is not seen in:
questions.solutionHtml:
Nucleus ambiguus

Special visceral efferent (SVE) fibers are the efferent nerve fibers that provide motor innervation to the muscles of the pharyngeal arches in humans.

  • The only nerves containing SVE fibers are: Trigeminal nerve (V), facial nerve (VII), glossopharyngeal nerve (IX), vagus nerve (X) and accessory nerve (XI).
  • Nucleus ambiguus contains the cell bodies of nerves that innervate the muscles of the soft palate, pharynx, and larynx which are strongly associated with speech and swallowing.
  • The axons of these cell bodies will form the tract and run in the ninth, tenth and eleventh cranial nerves.


BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 4, Page No.58, 59, 60.

questions.stem: Nerves supplying pharyngeal arches are developed from:
questions.solutionHtml:
Neural crest
  • Nerves supplying pharyngeal arches are developed from the cranial neural crest.


Langman's Medical Embryology , 14th Edition, Page No. 284,285,286, 287.

Inferior frontal gyrus

The inferior frontal gyrus includes the following areas:

  • Brodmann area 44
  • Brodmann area 45

Brodmann area 44 corresponds to Broca’s area (sometimes Broca’s area is taken to encompass Brodmann’s areas 44 and 45) — for the dominant hemisphere of the brain.



BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 4, Page No. 144.

Mesonephric duct
  • The ureteric bud is an outgrowth from the mesonephric duct, it has a separate opening into the urinary bladder. As the kidneys ascend, the ureters elongate and open into the bladder superiorly, while the roots of the mesonephric ducts are carried inferiorly, before fusing to form the trigone region
  • The ureteric bud also known as the metanephrogenic diverticulum is a protrusion from the mesonephric duct.


Langman's Medical Embryology , 14th Edition, Page No. 257.

questions.stemHtml: What is the feature of the muscle shown in the image below:
questions.solutionHtml:
Spiral

The muscle in the image is pectoralis major, which has spiral/ twisted fascicular arrangement.

  • Spiral or twisted fibers are also found in trapezius, latissimus dorsi and supinator.
  • Pectoralis major may also be called a convergent muscle (the fascicles extend from a broad, fan-shape area and converge on a single attachment site where the muscle interacts with a tendon).
  • In certain muscles the fasciculi are crossed. These are called cruciate muscles, e.g. sternocleidomastoid, masseter and adductor magnus.


BD Chaurasia's, Human Anatomy 8th Edition volume 1, Page No. 45,46.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is not true about iliolumbar ligament?

options.label: A
options.text: Upper fibers attached to the iliac crest

options.label: B
options.text: Lower fibers attached to the base of sacrum

options.label: C
options.text: Help in maintaining the lumbosacral joint stability

options.label: D
options.text: Upper attachment to transverse process of T12

questions.answerText: Upper attachment to transverse process of T12
questions.solutionHtml:
Upper attachment to transverse process of T12

The iliolumbar ligament is a strong ligament passing from the tip of the transverse process of the fifth lumbar vertebra to the posterior part of the inner lip of the iliac crest (upper margin of ilium).



Gray's Anatomy:The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice 42nd, Page No.842.

questions.stem: Which of the following structures develops from dorsal mesentery?
questions.solutionHtml:
Greater omentum
  • The derivatives of ventral mesentery are lesser omentum, falciform ligament, coronary ligament of liver and triangular ligament of liver.
  •  The derivatives of dorsal mesentery are greater omentum, gastrosplenic ligament, gastrocolic ligament, lienorenal ligament, mesentery of small intestine, mesoappendix, transverse mesocolon and sigmoid mesocolon.


Langman's Medical Embryology , 14th Edition, Page No.236, 237.
